summary: Landing this changes nothing: a new setting, off by default, `wait_for_peers_after_start = true` in config.toml, makes a fleet member wait after each start, before it starts, restarts, retires or records the end of any seat, until it has caught up with a peer, while still adopting live runtimes. After five minutes of waiting it raises an alert, and a person or an agent can let it go on without unreachable peers for that start with `st fleet admit-without` (a new member.admission-override claim)

schema.detail: New claim kind member.admission-override on host subjects (fields start, peers, reason; authorized-requester; append). No table change. Nothing writes it unless an operator runs `st fleet admit-without`.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: With the setting absent, as on every existing install, behaviour is unchanged. New route POST /v1/fleet/admission-override and command `st fleet admit-without`. An older member keeps a member.admission-override claim retryable until it upgrades, as it does for any unknown kind; nothing older reads it, and only the named member acts on it. An older build rejects a config.toml that has the new key.

downtime.detail: None while the setting is off. With it on, a restarted member's seat starts wait for its first complete exchange with a peer; running seats are adopted at once.

manual.detail: No manual step. To turn it on, add `wait_for_peers_after_start = true` to the member's config.toml and restart its daemon; remove the line before running an older build.

recovery.detail: Remove the line, or set it to false, and restart the daemon to act at once after a start again.
